svg.text: Woodward–Hoffmann notation, read in three parts
π: π bond / π system σ: σ bond ω: lone pair or empty p
not atoms: allyl cation (3 atoms) = 2; 1,3-dipole (3 atoms) = 4
③ letter = which faces the component uses
s = suprafacial (same face at both ends); a = antarafacial (opposite faces)
s vs a at a glance (green arrows = where the new bonds form)
both new bonds from the bottom face
one bond from the bottom, one from the top
σ bond (C–H, C–C, C–O) used on one side
one centre: lone pair (2 e⁻) or empty p (0 e⁻)
Step 1: classify each component by its electron count
π2 alkene, C=O; σ2 C–H, C–C, C–O; ω2 lone pair; allyl cation (3 atoms)
Step 2: count only these two kinds, then add
*HOMO ends: S = same sign at both ends, A = opposite (explanatory label, not lecture notation). Sources: L14 p.4–6; L15 p.13; Clayden 2e p.886–888.
